subject: Data retention exception - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention exception - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of your requirements from the call:
- PII minimization: FinCo needs no persistent storage of customer PII from inference requests (payment tokens, SSNs, email addresses).
- Data retention: preference for 0-retention on request payloads; if not possible for some routes, very short logs (24–72 hours) with automatic redaction.
- Logging controls: ability to turn on/off request logging per-route and have customer-controlled redaction/keys where feasible.
- Data residency: all logs and backups must remain in EU for EU customers (you mentioned EU region requirement for EU customer data).

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Offer an exception path: zero-persistence for request payloads (no long-term storage) for scoped routes; or
- Ephemeral logging with configurable retention (24/72 hours) and automated redaction;
- Customer-managed KMS options for certain artifacts;
- We’ll surface controls in the console and policy layer, but engineering & legal changes are required for contract-level commitments.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll loop in our security/legal folks for feasibility and timeline.
2) Redwood to share a DPA draft and our latest SOC2 report (attached).
3) If acceptable, we can scope implementation (engineering estimate) and produce contract language for the exception.

Could you confirm the priority (high/medium) and whether you need 0-retention for all routes or only specific ones (e.g., payment processing, identity lookups)? That will help us size the work.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with internal owners shortly.

—
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0184
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinCo Legal <legal@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:01:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention exception - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Camila — that matches what we discussed. Priority is high for FinCo; this is a gating item for the pilot. A few clarifications: 

- We need 0-retention for any field that could contain payment tokens or full SSNs. For other fields (free text), shortened logs (24 hours) are acceptable if automated redaction is applied.
- Can Redwood support per-route toggles so we can enable stricter retention for sensitive endpoints only?
- On customer-managed keys: we prefer that for anything that persists even temporarily.

Also: Legal would like to see the exact proposed contract language and your SOC2 report. If you can turn around a DPA amendment this week, we’ll review it and get back with redlines.

Appreciate the quick cadence — happy to hop on another quick call if that helps.

—
Alice Chen
Director, Platform Security, FinCo

Neha/Rafael — forwarding the FinCo requirements below (priority: high, pilot gating). Key asks: 0-retention for PII (payment tokens, SSNs), 24h short logs with automated redaction for free-text, per-route toggles, customer-managed KMS for any persisted artifacts, and EU residency for EU customers.

Can you confirm feasibility, any impacts to billing/metrics, and high-level engineering timeline? Also call out any compliance blockers. Rafael — can solutions engineering scope the per-route toggle work? Neha — what legal/compliance steps do we need to support a contractual exception?

Thanks — Camila

On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 3:08 PM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: ...
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:45:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Data retention exception - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for the context — we can support this, with tradeoffs and an implementation window. High level options: 

Option A — True 0-retention (no request payload persisted)
- Pros: aligns directly with FinCo ask.
- Cons: removes server-side request logs used for debugging and some billing reconciliations; metrics will need to be derived from aggregated telemetry (counts only).
- Effort: minimal pipeline gating and config flags; legal DPA amendment required.

Option B — Ephemeral logging + redaction (recommended shortest path)
- Behavior: keep request logs for 24 hours (configurable up to 72h), automatic PII redaction for configured fields, customer-managed KMS for any persisted artifacts.
- Pros: preserves short-term debugging capability and billing integrity while minimizing persistence.
- Cons: engineering work to add per-route toggles and redaction rules; must update retention policies and backup exclusions.
- Effort: ~6 weeks engineering + 2 weeks QA + legal review.

Compliance notes:
- We can guarantee data residency for logs by routing storage to EU buckets for EU tenant scopes.
- Any commitment to 0-retention or custom retention periods must be codified in the DPA (legal) and will require an exception approval from product/compliance.

Attachments: I’m attaching the latest SOC2 report and a DPA draft (redacted copy) for FinCo review.

Recommended next steps:
1) Offer FinCo Option B as the default (24h ephemeral + redaction) to unblock pilot faster.
2) Offer scope for route-level 0-retention for the most sensitive endpoints (payment, identity) as a contractual amendment.
3) Legal to prepare DPA amendment; engineering to start scoping per-route toggles.

I’ll coordinate timelines with Rafael & infra once you confirm.

—
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai

[Attachments: SOC2-Report-Redwood-2025.pdf, DPA_draft_redwood_v2.pdf]

Subject: Re: Data retention exception - post-call recap & next steps

Alice — thanks for the quick responses and for looping Legal. Per internal alignment, here’s the proposed plan to move forward: 

1) Implementation approach (recommended): Ephemeral logs (24 hours) + automated redaction for free-text fields; per-route 0-retention available for scoped sensitive endpoints (payment, identity) as a contractual exception.
2) Security has attached our SOC2 report and a DPA draft for your team to review (attached).
3) Timeline: we can provision the per-route controls + redaction rules in approx 6–8 weeks once requirements are finalized; legal DPA amendment to follow in parallel (1–2 weeks for a first draft).
4) For pilot: we can enable the 24-hour ephemeral + redaction immediately (config change) so you can start testing while we work on the per-route exceptions.

Next steps for FinCo:
- Please confirm you accept the pilot approach (24h ephemeral + redaction) so we can enable it this week.
- If you require route-level 0-retention for the pilot, confirm which endpoints and we’ll prioritize scoping.
- Legal: please review attached DPA draft and send redlines; we’ll route to our legal for negotiation.

I’ll set up a short follow-up call next week to review any redlines and timeline implications. Thanks — looking forward to getting this set up.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
